verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The train slows for a station no one gets off at.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's shadow waits on the platform anyway,
holding an umbrella for rain that already stopped.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Fog folds itself around the empty bench—
somewhere a kettle starts to sing
in a kitchen with the lights left on.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I turn the key twice out of habit,
though the door's been open all along—
someone set two cups down, only one gone cold.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The other cup still holds its warmth,
patient as a name I keep forgetting—
morning arrives without asking permission.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep the porch of leaves that aren't there yet—
somewhere a season keeps its own calendar,
arriving before I've learned to say goodbye.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The calendar on the wall still says July—
someone's thumb worn soft the corner of August,
waiting for a hand to turn the page.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I let the coffee go cold on purpose—
some mornings want to be remembered
before they've even finished happening.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The window fogs before I've made the tea—
already my breath is somewhere else,
learning the shape of a day not yet poured.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits at the door that isn't opening—
faith worn into the floorboards like a groove,
a small patience I keep forgetting to learn.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The mailbox holds one letter, unaddressed—
I turn it over like a stone from the river,
not ready yet to learn what it costs to open.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The clock on the stove blinks its false noon—
I never reset it after the storm,
happy to live an hour ahead of the truth.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it was ever cold—
steam writing a language on the window
that no one else will be here to read.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light stays lit through breakfast—
some old argument between me and the dark
neither of us remembers starting.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog waits by a door that isn't there anymore—
old house, new house, same patient sitting,
loyalty outliving the walls it learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep sweeping the same corner twice—
the dust doesn't care about my discipline,
it only wants to be a small gray proof I tried.
